title: From Business Requirements to Test Assertions: Evaluating LLM-Generated Oracles on Real Bugs
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.10277v1 (11 July 2026; full 4,938-word manuscript including data availability and references)
datasets: Defects4J Lang only: ten bugs, IDs 1 and 3–11. Buggy/fixed source diffs are manually translated into natural-language business requirements and a human-written requirement-derived oracle (REQ).
A manually designed test suite based on the business requirements and REQ evaluates each LLM oracle against both REQ and the actual system-under-test (SUT).
No BugsInPy or SWT-Bench experiment; no other Defects4J projects are included.
task: Generate Java test-oracle code from a business requirement and minimal package/class/method signature only, without source code, buggy/fixed diffs or input-output examples. Evaluate oracle correctness/generalization by agreement with a manually derived REQ oracle and by execution against buggy/fixed Defects4J Lang code (SUT target).
input_setting: Requirements-only oracle generation: prompts include method signature and manually written natural-language requirement. Authors first inspect buggy-to-fixed diffs to construct the requirements and REQ, but do not expose those diffs/source to the LLM. Five LLMs are evaluated.
author_relationship_evidence: The paper's Data Availability section explicitly links the Figshare share `50c240d183532de44c7a` and says it contains requirements, REQ, generated oracles, test suites and evaluation scripts. Figshare landing page title is “ESEM data,” describes exactly LLM-generated test oracles from business requirements on Defects4J Lang bugs 1 and 3–11, lists 171.51 MB and MIT license, but labels the item “shared privately.” Direct retrieval was inconsistent (one page load, then 403; download request returned HTTP 202 with zero bytes). Thus the link and claimed package exist, but the artifact is not verified as publicly downloadable in this audit.
source_commit_or_archive: Figshare private-share item candidate `https://figshare.com/s/50c240d183532de44c7a` (page states 171.51 MB, MIT; download link maps to file 64861545). No archive checksum or internal file listing verified because current requests return 403/202. Public Defects4J upstream remains available, but it does not contain the paper's manually authored requirements, REQ labels, test suites or scripts.
license: Figshare landing page lists MIT, but the item is marked shared privately and the archive contents/license file could not be inspected. Article is CC BY 4.0.
weights_status: The paper queries models via Together AI API and says model names/versions are documented in the replication package; exact immutable revisions and model-call prompts beyond paper templates are not verified because the Figshare archive is inaccessible. No model calls or weights retrieved.
evaluation_route: Read all 4,938 words / 492 extracted lines. Paper reports a 10-bug pilot on Defects4J Lang; DeepSeek-V3 macro-F1 is 0.7476 against SUT and 0.8179 against REQ; Qwen3-Coder-480B is 0.7030 against SUT and 0.7779 against REQ. Mistral-7B compiles on only 9 of 10 bug cases. REQ alignment is consistently higher than SUT alignment for most models; technicality/ambiguity correlations are near zero with wide confidence intervals. The authors claim the Figshare package contains business requirements, REQ, model-generated oracles, test suites and evaluation scripts, potentially allowing reruns without reproducing generation. However, the link-only Figshare item is marked private and file download did not succeed in this audit, so the own-model route is not presently verified. No source/model run.
blockers: The only artifact link is a Figshare private-share item. Although its landing page describes a 171.51 MB MIT package, direct requests were inconsistent (403/202) and no archive contents/checksum could be verified.
The study has only ten bugs from one Defects4J project (Lang), so even if the package is obtained it is a small pilot and does not support broad claims about bug classes or project generalization.

The method depends on manually constructed business requirements and REQ oracles; without the package, these subjective labels and test suites cannot be independently reconstructed without reimplementing the study.
Models are accessed via Together AI and exact immutable revisions are not verified; the largest model is Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8, unlike the user's local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B.
The correlation analysis uses n=10 and wide 95% confidence intervals; null correlation should be treated as low-powered preliminary evidence, not proof that ambiguity/technicality do not matter.
concept_fit: Very high conceptual fit for specification/requirement-driven oracle generation and Defects4J: it explicitly separates intended behavior (REQ) from observed implementation behavior (SUT), highlighting that a test can match prose yet disagree with code. Manual diff-to-business-requirement construction connects code changes to behavior. It does not localize/root-cause bugs or generate issue-reproduction tests directly; no root-cause taxonomy is provided.
recommendation: Promote as a high-fit Defects4J oracle paper but not yet as a reproducible base. Its requirements-only input, REQ-vs-SUT comparison, and explicit warning that specification alignment differs from implementation alignment are valuable for concept/oracle research. The paper claims a complete MIT Figshare package, but the only share is marked private and the archive download failed in this audit; verify access before relying on it or planning a local-Qwen evaluation. The pilot has only ten Lang bugs, so use as a protocol seed rather than broad benchmark evidence. No code or API calls.
supporting_locations: Paper Sections 3–4: manual buggy/fixed diff-to-business-requirement process, REQ oracle, requirements-only prompts and 10 Defects4J Lang bugs.
Paper Tables 1–3: requirement ratings, per-bug results and model-by-target macro metrics; DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-Coder results.
Paper Sections 6.3–6.4: manual construction subjectivity, single-project/small-n threat, and proposed use as assistive oracle drafting.
Paper Data Availability section explicitly states the Figshare package should include requirements, REQ, generated oracles, test suites and scripts.

Figshare page identifies ESEM data / Defects4J Lang bugs 1,3–11, 171.51 MB and MIT, while marking it as shared privately; shell download returned HTTP 202 with zero bytes and browser later returned 403.
